Forecast Discussion

High pressure sits right on top of us Monday. The air under a high sinks, and sinking air dries out and clears out. That is the whole story this week. The air over the mountains is the driest we have measured this fall, and it stays that way through the weekend. One other effect of this dry air... No night this week is safe from frost or a freeze in the protected valleys.

The high slides to New England Tuesday. A northeast breeze follows, and a few high clouds drift through from the west. A storm passes well off the Carolina coast Tuesday and Wednesday. It stays out to sea.

Wednesday and Thursday are seasonal, sunny days. A fresh batch of cool air drops in from the north Friday night into Saturday with no front to mark it. Saturday morning is the coldest of the week, with freezing temperatures in the valleys.

The next high settles over us Saturday and Sunday. Afternoons warm back up by Sunday under full sun.

The next chance for rain does not show up until the end of the month at the earliest. Enjoy a week of fall at its best.
